To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oxytocin and/or vasopressin, when injected intravenously in the amount of 20 IU, cause increase in diuresis in dehydrated cows, provided that the cows are not hyperhydrated, and that oxytocin, in the amount of about 0.34 IU per minute, when given intravenously for 3 hours, does not cause water intoxications in hyperhydrated cattle, though plasma osmotic pressure drops to 244 mosmo/kg.

oxytocin and, to a lesser degree, vasopressin may be used to induce diuresis increase in lactating cows, and, if the animals are hyperhydrated, the diuresis increase is accompanied by saluresis, and, if water intoxication is induced, the diureses increase is followed by saluresis inhibition.
oxytocin and arginine vasopressin cause antidiuresis, and that oxytocin is able to increase diuresis in dehydrated and rehydrated cows, but not in hyperhydrated ones.

a study of oxytocin and/or vasopressin effects on water diuresis in cows, and the effects are evaluated in relation to the water status of the animals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

oxytocin and/or vasopressin, when administered in the form of intravenous injection or continuous infusion, are not able to induce water intoxication in cows, even when they are in hyperhydrated state.
oxytocin does not cause water intoxications in cows.

oxytocin and/or vasopressin, in the form of neurohypophyseus extract preparations or synthetical preparations, do not cause antidiuresis, if given to lactating cows, which have undergone twelve hours of dehydration and have not been rehydrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antidiuresis effect of oxytocin and of vasopressin is a consequence of the increase in the osmotic pressure of the blood plasma and of the increase in Na+ concentration.

oxytocin and/or vasopressin may be applied in dehydrated cows for the purpose of increasing diuresis and saluretic effects, and in hyperhydrated animals for the purpose of inhibiting diuresis and reducing the saluretic effect, but not for the purpose of producing antidiuresis in dehydrated or hyperhydrated cows.
oxytocin and/or vasopressin may cause water intoxication only when they are given to cows that have undergone water withdrawal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

oxytocin and, to a lesser degree, vasopressin, are capable of blocking water diuresis in lactating cows, and that this effect is associated with the ability of oxytocin to induce antidiuresis, which is a prerequisite for the onset of the saluresis.
oxytocin and its derivatives may cause diuresis increase in lactating cows and, in addition, they may cause water intoxication.
oxytocin is not a diuretic hormone in cows.
